key_insight: Two commonly conflated block-sparse objectives have different exact models and can yield different maximizers; safeguarded A-SQ ascent supports convergence and finite support identification under a strict threshold margin.
engineering_relevance: The corrected formulation provides a principled basis for sparse feature extraction, with explicit edge-case handling and locally justified safe screening.
method: Derive A-SUM from normalized loading balls and A-SQ from a quadratic lift.
Use safeguarded Riemannian ascent on the Stiefel manifold, with explicit tie, zero-response, rank-deficiency, and refitting conventions.
Analyze post-identification dynamics using active-covariance power iteration or a coupled polar-map derivative.
evidence_signal: Planted-spike tests match predicted identification times and local rates; AI-panel tests report PCA-level reconstruction with improved interpretability, while three scRNA datasets show AMI gains of 0.023–0.044 over dense PCA at matched sparsity.
watch_item: The convergence guarantee applies to safeguarded ascent, not the historical full-polar iteration, and finite support identification requires a strict threshold margin.
paper_title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics
